antidotes.why: Discernment tells the good from the pleasant to cure confusion.
Good company brings discernment and removes doubt and delusion over time.
The wish to understand answers confusion by having Arjuna ask those who have seen.
The Manas gives devotion as the herb for the root illness.

chains.summary: Seeing his own people, Arjuna is overcome and his limbs fail. He drops the bow and sits down in grief. He cannot tell which course is better. Confused about what is right, he asks to be taught.
chains.title: Arjuna's collapse

verses.m: Arjuna said: Krishna, when I see my own people standing here, eager to fight, I am overcome with pity and sorrow.
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकृपया परयाऽऽविष्टो विषीदन्निदमब्रवीत् । दृष्ट्वेमं स्वजनं कृष्ण युयुत्सुं समुपस्थितम् ॥

verses.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
verses.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥

verses.m: Sanjaya said: Having spoken this on the battlefield, Arjuna sank down on the seat of the chariot, letting fall his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥

chains.summary: Arjuna asks what pushes a person to do wrong against their own wish. Krishna says it is desire and anger born of rajas, and this covers knowing as smoke covers fire and dust covers a mirror.
chains.title: What drives us against our will

verses.m: Arjuna said: Then what drives a person to do wrong, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचअथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः । अनिच्छन्नपि वार्ष्णेय बलादिव नियोजितः ॥

verses.m: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion; all-devouring and greatly harmful. Know this to be the enemy here.
verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकाम एष क्रोध एष रजोगुणसमुद्भवः । महाशनो महापाप्मा विद्ध्येनमिह वैरिणम् ॥

verses.m: As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and an embryo by the womb, so is this wisdom covered by desire.
verses.sa: धूमेनाव्रियते वह्निर्यथाऽऽदर्शो मलेन च । यथोल्बेनावृतो गर्भस्तथा तेनेदमावृतम् ॥

chains.summary: Sattva produces knowledge. Rajas produces greed. Tamas produces heedlessness, delusion and ignorance. Tamas binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep. When rajas rules there is greed, restless activity and craving.
chains.title: What each guna yields

verses.m: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
verses.sa: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥

verses.m: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness and craving: these arise when rajas increases, best of the Bharatas.
verses.sa: लोभः प्रवृत्तिरारम्भः कर्मणामशमः स्पृहा । रजस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे भरतर्षभ ॥

verses.m: Darkness, inertia, heedlessness and delusion: these arise when tamas increases, joy of the Kurus.
verses.sa: अप्रकाशोऽप्रवृत्तिश्च प्रमादो मोह एव च । तमस्येतानि जायन्ते विवृद्धे कुरुनन्दन ॥

chains.summary: Dwelling on an object breeds attachment. Attachment breeds desire. Desire breeds anger. Anger breeds delusion. Delusion causes loss of memory. Loss of memory ruins judgement. With judgement gone, one is lost.
chains.title: The ladder of fall

verses.m: When a person dwells on objects, attachment to them is born. From attachment comes desire, and from desire, anger.
verses.sa: ध्यायतो विषयान्पुंसः सङ्गस्तेषूपजायते । सङ्गात् संजायते कामः कामात्क्रोधोऽभिजायते ॥

verses.m: From anger comes delusion; from delusion, confusion of memory; from confusion of memory, the ruin of understanding; and with understanding ruined, a person is lost.
verses.sa: क्रोधाद्भवति संमोहः संमोहात्स्मृतिविभ्रमः । स्मृतिभ्रंशाद् बुद्धिनाशो बुद्धिनाशात्प्रणश्यति ॥

depicts.m: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
depicts.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
depicts.why: Shows the mind confused about dharma.

depicts.m: Let the moth fall into the blazing flame not knowing that it burns; let the fish swallow the bait not knowing the hook. But we, knowing full well, still do not let go of desires tangled in a net of dangers. Ah, how deep is the power of delusion!
depicts.sa: अजानन्दाहात्म्यं पततु शलभस्तीव्रदहने स मीनोऽप्यज्ञानाद्वडिशयुतमश्नातु पिशितम् । विजानन्तोऽप्येते वयमिह विपज्जालजटिलान् न मुञ्चामः कामानहह गहनो मोहमहिमा ॥
depicts.why: Knowing it harms and doing it anyway.

depicts.m: As a man brought blindfolded from Gandhara and left in a deserted place might wander east or north or south, crying, 'I was brought here blindfolded and left blindfolded,' and someone removes his blindfold and says, 'Gandhara is that way, go that way,' and asking from village to village, informed and sensible, he reaches Gandhara; so a person who has a teacher comes to know.
depicts.sa: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्योऽभिनद्धाक्षमानीय तं ततोऽतिजने विसृजेत्स यथा तत्र प्राङ्वोदङ्वाधराङ्वा प्रत्यङ्वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतोऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥ तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयादेतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति स ग्रामाद्ग्रामं पृच्छन्पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारानेवोपसम्पद्येतैवमेवेहाचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेव चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्येऽथ सम्पत्स्य इति ॥
depicts.why: Brought here blindfolded and left, turning every way and calling out.

depicts.m: My limbs give way, my mouth is parched, my body trembles and my hair stands on end.
depicts.sa: सीदन्ति मम गात्राणि मुखं च परिशुष्यति । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च जायते ॥
depicts.why: Shows the mind whirling from inside.

depicts.m: With these seemingly mixed words you confuse my mind. Tell me decisively that one thing by which I may reach the highest good.
depicts.sa: व्यामिश्रेणेव वाक्येन बुद्धिं मोहयसीव मे । तदेकं वद निश्िचत्य येन श्रेयोऽहमाप्नुयाम् ॥

depicts.m: I take refuge at your lotus feet, Lord, which free one from the world and which yogis meditate on. Teach me so that I may easily and happily cross this endless ocean of ignorance.
depicts.sa: अहं प्रपन्नोऽस्मि पदाम्बुजं प्रभो भवापवर्गं तव योगिभावितम् । यथाञ्जसाज्ञानमपारवारिधिं सुखं तरिष्यामि तथानुशाधि माम् ॥
depicts.why: Shows the ocean of ignorance he feels himself in.

depicts.m: 'Can one whose home is beneath the wishing tree suffer the pain of poverty? Thinking this over in your heart, Moon-crowned Lord, take away the heavy confusion of my mind.'
depicts.sa: जासु भवनु सुरतरु तर होई। सहि कि दरिद्र जनित दुखु सोई॥ ससिभूषन अस हृदयँ बिचारी। हरहु नाथ मम मति भ्रम भारी ॥
depicts.why: Depicts a heavy confusion she cannot clear alone.

depicts.m: On the same tree a person sits sunk, grieving, bewildered by his own helplessness. When he sees the other, the content lord, and his greatness, his sorrow leaves him.
depicts.sa: समाने वृक्षे पुरुषो निमग्नोऽनिशया शोचति मुह्यमानः । जुष्टं यदा पश्यत्यन्यमीशमस्य महिमानमिति वीतशोकः ॥

gloss: Judgement is clouded so that right and wrong, mine and not mine, blur. The Gita ends when this lifts, as the Gita says in verse 18.73.

heals.m: My nature is stricken by weakness and my mind is confused about what is right. I ask you: tell me for certain what is best for me. I am your student; I have come to you, teach me.
heals.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥

heals.m: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
heals.sa: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥

heals.m: Without good company there is no clear judgement, and by Ram's grace alone such company comes easily. Good company is the root of joy and well-being; finding it is the fruit, and every other practice is only the flower.
heals.sa: बिनु सतसंग बिबेक न होई। राम कृपा बिनु सुलभ न सोई॥ सतसंगत मुद मंगल मूला। सोई फल सिधि सब साधन फूला ॥
heals.why: Names confusion partly a matter of whose company one keeps.

heals.m: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
heals.sa: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥
heals.why: Gives the many pains one root.

heals.m: You met me on the road; how can I explain it to you in passing? All doubts end only when one spends a long time in good company.
heals.sa: मिलेहु गरुड़ मारग महँ मोही। कवन भाँति समुझावौं तोही॥ तबहिं होइ सब संसय भंगा। जब बहु काल करिअ सतसंगा ॥

heals.m: The good and the pleasant both come to a person. The wise one examines them and tells them apart. The wise chooses the good over the pleasant; the dull chooses the pleasant, for getting and keeping.
heals.sa: श्रेयश्च प्रेयश्च मनुष्यमेतस्तौ सम्परीत्य विविनक्ति धीर:। श्रेयो हि धीरोऽभि प्रेयसो वृणीते प्रेयो मन्दो योगक्षेमाद् वृणीते ॥

heals.m: The wise do not long for what cannot be had, do not choose to keep grieving over what is lost, and do not lose their heads in misfortune.
heals.sa: नाप्राप्यमभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् / आपत्सु च न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डितबुद्धयः

heals.m: As a man brought blindfolded from Gandhara and left in a deserted place might wander east or north or south, crying, 'I was brought here blindfolded and left blindfolded,' and someone removes his blindfold and says, 'Gandhara is that way, go that way,' and asking from village to village, informed and sensible, he reaches Gandhara; so a person who has a teacher comes to know.
heals.sa: यथा सोम्य पुरुषं गन्धारेभ्योऽभिनद्धाक्षमानीय तं ततोऽतिजने विसृजेत्स यथा तत्र प्राङ्वोदङ्वाधराङ्वा प्रत्यङ्वा प्रध्मायीताभिनद्धाक्ष आनीतोऽभिनद्धाक्षो विसृष्टः ॥ तस्य यथाभिनहनं प्रमुच्य प्रब्रूयादेतां दिशं गन्धारा एतां दिशं व्रजेति स ग्रामाद्ग्रामं पृच्छन्पण्डितो मेधावी गन्धारानेवोपसम्पद्येतैवमेवेहाचार्यवान्पुरुषो वेद तस्य तावदेव चिरं यावन्न विमोक्ष्येऽथ सम्पत्स्य इति ॥
heals.why: Shows being lost as a blindfold that can be untied and the way home asked for.

hero.m: When your understanding crosses the mire of delusion, you will grow indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
hero.sa: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥

loci.m: When your understanding crosses the mire of delusion, you will grow indifferent to all that you have heard and all that is yet to be heard.
loci.sa: यदा ते मोहकलिलं बुद्धिर्व्यतितरिष्यति । तदा गन्तासि निर्वेदं श्रोतव्यस्य श्रुतस्य च ॥

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows devotion as what makes the gift.

practices.m: Whether a task is good or bad, a wise person should first carefully weigh its outcome. The result of deeds done in great haste burns the heart like a thorn until one's dying day.
practices.sa: गुणवदगुणवद्वा कुर्वता कार्यजातं परिणतिरवधार्या यत्नतः पण्डितेन । अतिरभसकृतानां कर्मणामाविपत्ते- र्भवति हृदयदाही शल्यतुल्यो विपाकः ॥

practices.m: Good company takes dullness from the mind, sprinkles truth into speech, raises one's dignity, removes wrongdoing, clears the heart and spreads one's good name in every direction. Tell me, what does good company not do for a person?
practices.sa: जाड्यं धियो हरति सिञ्चति वाचि सत्यं मानोन्नतिं दिशति पापमपाकरोति । चेतः प्रसादयति दिक्षु तनोति कीर्तिं सत्सङ्गतिः कथय किं न करोति पुंसाम् ॥
practices.why: Shows removal of dullness of mind.

practices.m: Friend chataka, listen carefully for a moment. Many clouds live in the sky, but not all are alike. Some drench the earth with rain; some only thunder for nothing. Do not speak pleading words before every cloud you see.
practices.sa: रे रे चातक सावधानमनसा मित्र क्षणं श्रूयताम् अम्भोदा बहवो वसन्ति गगने सर्वेऽपि नैकादृशाः । केचिद्वृष्टिभिरार्द्रयन्ति धरणीं गर्जन्ति केचिद्वृथा यं यं पश्यसि तस्य तस्य पुरतो मा ब्रूहि दीनं वचः ॥
practices.why: Names tell the giver from the thunderer.

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Make a friend slowly, and give one up slowly. A friendship made slowly is one that lasts long.
practices.sa: चिरेण मित्रं बध्नीयाच्चिरेण च कृतं त्यजेत् / चिरेण हि कृतं मित्रं चिरं धारणमर्हति
practices.why: Take time before binding or breaking a bond.

practices.m: Heal the pain of the mind with wisdom and the pain of the body with medicine. That is what knowledge can do; don't behave like a child about it.
practices.sa: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः / एतद्विज्ञानमसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात्

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.

stories.l: Clarity, once found, turns into action.
stories.s: Krishna asks if Arjuna's confusion is gone; Arjuna says yes and that he will act. Sanjaya rejoices and declares that where Krishna and Arjuna stand, victory follows.

stories.l: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
stories.s: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
stories.t: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free

stories.l: There is a calm witness in you that the anxious part can turn to.
stories.s: Two birds sit on one tree: one eats the fruit and grieves, the other simply watches. When the anxious bird sees the calm one beside it, its sorrow falls away. The section goes on to praise truth, effort and freedom from craving.

stories.l: Seeing clearly can feel like waking up: nothing changed outside, everything changed inside.
stories.s: Hearing the first teaching, Janaka bursts into wonder: he sees he has been fooled by confusion for years. He describes owning nothing and everything, and losing his fear.
